        Idea:
Sprint 2 of the megaplan cloud feature — extend core megaplan ergonomics, add local + ssh providers, ship toolchain extensibility in cloud.yaml, retire the old reigh-megaplan-dev folder.

### Context
Sprint 1 shipped in v0.19.0 on 2026-04-21: built-in megaplan cloud subcommand (init/build/deploy/status/attach/logs/exec/resume/down/destroy) with a Railway provider, extracted from the ad-hoc setup at ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/. Spec schema lives in megaplan/cloud/spec.py, templates in megaplan/cloud/templates/, providers in megaplan/cloud/providers/.

Architectural principle established in sprint 1 and now codified: CORE megaplan owns capabilities, CLOUD subcommands are thin transport wrappers. Do not reinvent chain state parsing in cloud. Do not grow a parallel 'cloud chain *' surface. Core gets the command; cloud wraps it for remote execution.

### Sprint 2 deliverables

Core megaplan additions (must work locally without any cloud dependency):
1. megaplan chain start --spec <path> — validate spec, resolve referenced idea files, kick auto-loop per milestone. Replaces the 'init + auto' pair for chain runs.
2. megaplan chain status --spec <path> — read chain_state.json, pretty-print current_milestone, completed, remaining, per-milestone status. Unit tests against synthetic chain states.
3. megaplan init --idea-file <path> with optional --auto-start flag — read idea from a file instead of the positional CLI arg.

Cloud additions (thin wrappers over the new core commands):
4. megaplan cloud chain <spec.yaml> — upload spec, then cloud exec to call megaplan chain start remotely.
5. megaplan cloud bootstrap <idea-file> — upload idea file, then cloud exec to call megaplan init --idea-file --auto-start remotely.
6. megaplan cloud status --chain — fetch remote chain_state.json, invoke the core chain-status formatter on it. Do NOT reinvent the parser.

New providers:
7. Local provider (docker compose) — fastest iteration target, no Railway/cloud dependency. Becomes the CI-friendly smoke-test target.
8. SSH provider (plain docker-over-ssh) — 'any host with docker + ssh access' story.

Toolchain extensibility:
9. toolchains: block in cloud.yaml — declares one or more toolchains (rust, go, java, or custom with user-provided install snippet). Template renderer appends corresponding Dockerfile stages. Without this, the image is Python/Node only.

Hardening + retirement:
10. Secret redaction in cloud logs output (match known secret name patterns, replace with ***REDACTED***).
11. Clear error messages + documentation link when railway or docker CLI is missing at runtime.
12. ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ migration — deploy cloud with a cloud.yaml matching reigh's current env, run a tiny plan to verify parity, then delete the folder and replace with a MIGRATED.md pointer.

### Hard constraints
- Core commands MUST work locally without any cloud code loaded.
- Cloud wrappers MUST call out to core commands, not reimplement.
- Fly provider is OPTIONAL (skip if time-pressured).
- Preserve v0.19.0's public surface; this is additive.
- No breaking cloud.yaml changes from v0.19.0 (add fields, don't rename).
- Unit tests for every new core command; mocked-subprocess tests for every new provider; smoke test for local provider docker-compose lifecycle.

### Explicit non-goals
- No Kubernetes provider.
- No chain-of-chains.
- No cloud-specific chain status parser (the whole point of the core-first architecture).
- No version bump in this plan — sprint 2 ships as v0.20.0 but the bump + CHANGELOG commit is a separate follow-up.

### References
- Sprint 1 landed in v0.19.0 (2026-04-21). Full CHANGELOG entry in CHANGELOG.md.
- Reigh parity reference: ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ and megaplan/cloud/_reference/ (gitignored local copy of same).
- Verified launcher: ./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan (system python is 3.8, fails on NotRequired).
- Sprint 1 target retrospective: cloud subcommand CLI is already wired via megaplan/cloud/cli.py and dispatched from megaplan/cli.py.

Robustness: standard — feature-rich with architecture decisions to enforce, multiple independent pieces worth independent critique, gate useful for scope discipline.

    "Validation Order step 7 has a known text-level mismatch (accepted tradeoff): plan writes `cloud bootstrap` + `cloud status --chain` via marker as a single sequence, but `cloud bootstrap` never writes a marker.     "Marker location MUST be provider-independent: `~/.megaplan/cloud/markers/<sha256(abs_path_of_cloud.yaml)[:16]>/last_chain.json`.     "argv normalization MUST be the first line of `main()` in `megaplan/cli.py`. `cli_entry()` calls `main(argv=None)`; without `if argv is None: argv = sys.argv[1:]` at entry, the lazy `argv[0] == 'cloud'` intercept never fires for shell invocations. `tests/test_cli_entry.py` regression-guards this \u2014 do not delete it.",
    "Core/cloud isolation is a grep-enforced invariant. No `megaplan.cloud.*` import may appear in any core module. No cloud module may reimplement chain-state parsing beyond calling `chain.load_chain_state` / `chain.load_spec` / `chain.format_chain_status`. T20's grep check enforces this.",
    "Public `cloud.yaml` surface from v0.19.0 must parse unchanged \u2014 every v0.19.0 spec loads with no change in parsed `CloudSpec` fields. All additions (local/ssh blocks, toolchains) are additive with defaults.",
    "With `toolchains:` OMITTED, the rendered Dockerfile must be byte-identical to the v0.19.0 baseline. This is a byte-diff test, not a semantic-equivalence test \u2014 trailing newlines, whitespace, and comment order all count.",
    "`cloud bootstrap --plan-name` is OPTIONAL. When omitted, the remote command must NOT include `--name` \u2014 delegate to core's slug-based default. When set, include `--name {shlex.quote(args.plan_name)}`.",
    "Every interpolated value in SSH provider argv and `ssh_exec` call sites must pass through `shlex.quote`. This is a shell-injection surface; tests should assert quoting with adversarial inputs containing spaces, quotes, and `$`.",

        Idea:
Sprint 2 of the megaplan cloud feature — extend core megaplan ergonomics, add local + ssh providers, ship toolchain extensibility in cloud.yaml, retire the old reigh-megaplan-dev folder.

### Context
Sprint 1 shipped in v0.19.0 on 2026-04-21: built-in megaplan cloud subcommand (init/build/deploy/status/attach/logs/exec/resume/down/destroy) with a Railway provider, extracted from the ad-hoc setup at ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/. Spec schema lives in megaplan/cloud/spec.py, templates in megaplan/cloud/templates/, providers in megaplan/cloud/providers/.

Architectural principle established in sprint 1 and now codified: CORE megaplan owns capabilities, CLOUD subcommands are thin transport wrappers. Do not reinvent chain state parsing in cloud. Do not grow a parallel 'cloud chain *' surface. Core gets the command; cloud wraps it for remote execution.

### Sprint 2 deliverables

Core megaplan additions (must work locally without any cloud dependency):
1. megaplan chain start --spec <path> — validate spec, resolve referenced idea files, kick auto-loop per milestone. Replaces the 'init + auto' pair for chain runs.
2. megaplan chain status --spec <path> — read chain_state.json, pretty-print current_milestone, completed, remaining, per-milestone status. Unit tests against synthetic chain states.
3. megaplan init --idea-file <path> with optional --auto-start flag — read idea from a file instead of the positional CLI arg.

Cloud additions (thin wrappers over the new core commands):
4. megaplan cloud chain <spec.yaml> — upload spec, then cloud exec to call megaplan chain start remotely.
5. megaplan cloud bootstrap <idea-file> — upload idea file, then cloud exec to call megaplan init --idea-file --auto-start remotely.
6. megaplan cloud status --chain — fetch remote chain_state.json, invoke the core chain-status formatter on it. Do NOT reinvent the parser.

New providers:
7. Local provider (docker compose) — fastest iteration target, no Railway/cloud dependency. Becomes the CI-friendly smoke-test target.
8. SSH provider (plain docker-over-ssh) — 'any host with docker + ssh access' story.

Toolchain extensibility:
9. toolchains: block in cloud.yaml — declares one or more toolchains (rust, go, java, or custom with user-provided install snippet). Template renderer appends corresponding Dockerfile stages. Without this, the image is Python/Node only.

Hardening + retirement:
10. Secret redaction in cloud logs output (match known secret name patterns, replace with ***REDACTED***).
11. Clear error messages + documentation link when railway or docker CLI is missing at runtime.
12. ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ migration — deploy cloud with a cloud.yaml matching reigh's current env, run a tiny plan to verify parity, then delete the folder and replace with a MIGRATED.md pointer.

### Hard constraints
- Core commands MUST work locally without any cloud code loaded.
- Cloud wrappers MUST call out to core commands, not reimplement.
- Fly provider is OPTIONAL (skip if time-pressured).
- Preserve v0.19.0's public surface; this is additive.
- No breaking cloud.yaml changes from v0.19.0 (add fields, don't rename).
- Unit tests for every new core command; mocked-subprocess tests for every new provider; smoke test for local provider docker-compose lifecycle.

### Explicit non-goals
- No Kubernetes provider.
- No chain-of-chains.
- No cloud-specific chain status parser (the whole point of the core-first architecture).
- No version bump in this plan — sprint 2 ships as v0.20.0 but the bump + CHANGELOG commit is a separate follow-up.

### References
- Sprint 1 landed in v0.19.0 (2026-04-21). Full CHANGELOG entry in CHANGELOG.md.
- Reigh parity reference: ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ and megaplan/cloud/_reference/ (gitignored local copy of same).
- Verified launcher: ./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan (system python is 3.8, fails on NotRequired).
- Sprint 1 target retrospective: cloud subcommand CLI is already wired via megaplan/cloud/cli.py and dispatched from megaplan/cli.py.

Robustness: standard — feature-rich with architecture decisions to enforce, multiple independent pieces worth independent critique, gate useful for scope discipline.

        Idea:
Sprint 2 of the megaplan cloud feature — extend core megaplan ergonomics, add local + ssh providers, ship toolchain extensibility in cloud.yaml, retire the old reigh-megaplan-dev folder.

### Context
Sprint 1 shipped in v0.19.0 on 2026-04-21: built-in megaplan cloud subcommand (init/build/deploy/status/attach/logs/exec/resume/down/destroy) with a Railway provider, extracted from the ad-hoc setup at ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/. Spec schema lives in megaplan/cloud/spec.py, templates in megaplan/cloud/templates/, providers in megaplan/cloud/providers/.

Architectural principle established in sprint 1 and now codified: CORE megaplan owns capabilities, CLOUD subcommands are thin transport wrappers. Do not reinvent chain state parsing in cloud. Do not grow a parallel 'cloud chain *' surface. Core gets the command; cloud wraps it for remote execution.

### Sprint 2 deliverables

Core megaplan additions (must work locally without any cloud dependency):
1. megaplan chain start --spec <path> — validate spec, resolve referenced idea files, kick auto-loop per milestone. Replaces the 'init + auto' pair for chain runs.
2. megaplan chain status --spec <path> — read chain_state.json, pretty-print current_milestone, completed, remaining, per-milestone status. Unit tests against synthetic chain states.
3. megaplan init --idea-file <path> with optional --auto-start flag — read idea from a file instead of the positional CLI arg.

Cloud additions (thin wrappers over the new core commands):
4. megaplan cloud chain <spec.yaml> — upload spec, then cloud exec to call megaplan chain start remotely.
5. megaplan cloud bootstrap <idea-file> — upload idea file, then cloud exec to call megaplan init --idea-file --auto-start remotely.
6. megaplan cloud status --chain — fetch remote chain_state.json, invoke the core chain-status formatter on it. Do NOT reinvent the parser.

New providers:
7. Local provider (docker compose) — fastest iteration target, no Railway/cloud dependency. Becomes the CI-friendly smoke-test target.
8. SSH provider (plain docker-over-ssh) — 'any host with docker + ssh access' story.

Toolchain extensibility:
9. toolchains: block in cloud.yaml — declares one or more toolchains (rust, go, java, or custom with user-provided install snippet). Template renderer appends corresponding Dockerfile stages. Without this, the image is Python/Node only.

Hardening + retirement:
10. Secret redaction in cloud logs output (match known secret name patterns, replace with ***REDACTED***).
11. Clear error messages + documentation link when railway or docker CLI is missing at runtime.
12. ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ migration — deploy cloud with a cloud.yaml matching reigh's current env, run a tiny plan to verify parity, then delete the folder and replace with a MIGRATED.md pointer.

### Hard constraints
- Core commands MUST work locally without any cloud code loaded.
- Cloud wrappers MUST call out to core commands, not reimplement.
- Fly provider is OPTIONAL (skip if time-pressured).
- Preserve v0.19.0's public surface; this is additive.
- No breaking cloud.yaml changes from v0.19.0 (add fields, don't rename).
- Unit tests for every new core command; mocked-subprocess tests for every new provider; smoke test for local provider docker-compose lifecycle.

### Explicit non-goals
- No Kubernetes provider.
- No chain-of-chains.
- No cloud-specific chain status parser (the whole point of the core-first architecture).
- No version bump in this plan — sprint 2 ships as v0.20.0 but the bump + CHANGELOG commit is a separate follow-up.

### References
- Sprint 1 landed in v0.19.0 (2026-04-21). Full CHANGELOG entry in CHANGELOG.md.
- Reigh parity reference: ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ and megaplan/cloud/_reference/ (gitignored local copy of same).
- Verified launcher: ./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan (system python is 3.8, fails on NotRequired).
- Sprint 1 target retrospective: cloud subcommand CLI is already wired via megaplan/cloud/cli.py and dispatched from megaplan/cli.py.

Robustness: standard — feature-rich with architecture decisions to enforce, multiple independent pieces worth independent critique, gate useful for scope discipline.

    "Marker location MUST be provider-independent: `~/.megaplan/cloud/markers/<sha256(abs_path_of_cloud.yaml)[:16]>/last_chain.json`.     "Core/cloud isolation is a grep-enforced invariant. No `megaplan.cloud.*` import may appear in any core module. No cloud module may reimplement chain-state parsing beyond calling `chain.load_chain_state` / `chain.load_spec` / `chain.format_chain_status`. T20's grep check enforces this.",

    "`cloud bootstrap --plan-name` is OPTIONAL. When omitted, the remote command must NOT include `--name` \u2014 delegate to core's slug-based default. When set, include `--name {shlex.quote(args.plan_name)}`.",

> DEVELOPER

Execute the approved plan in the repository.

        Project directory:
        /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan

        Idea:
Sprint 2 of the megaplan cloud feature — extend core megaplan ergonomics, add local + ssh providers, ship toolchain extensibility in cloud.yaml, retire the old reigh-megaplan-dev folder.

### Context
Sprint 1 shipped in v0.19.0 on 2026-04-21: built-in megaplan cloud subcommand (init/build/deploy/status/attach/logs/exec/resume/down/destroy) with a Railway provider, extracted from the ad-hoc setup at ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/. Spec schema lives in megaplan/cloud/spec.py, templates in megaplan/cloud/templates/, providers in megaplan/cloud/providers/.

Architectural principle established in sprint 1 and now codified: CORE megaplan owns capabilities, CLOUD subcommands are thin transport wrappers. Do not reinvent chain state parsing in cloud. Do not grow a parallel 'cloud chain *' surface. Core gets the command; cloud wraps it for remote execution.

### Sprint 2 deliverables

Core megaplan additions (must work locally without any cloud dependency):
1. megaplan chain start --spec <path> — validate spec, resolve referenced idea files, kick auto-loop per milestone. Replaces the 'init + auto' pair for chain runs.
2. megaplan chain status --spec <path> — read chain_state.json, pretty-print current_milestone, completed, remaining, per-milestone status. Unit tests against synthetic chain states.
3. megaplan init --idea-file <path> with optional --auto-start flag — read idea from a file instead of the positional CLI arg.

Cloud additions (thin wrappers over the new core commands):
4. megaplan cloud chain <spec.yaml> — upload spec, then cloud exec to call megaplan chain start remotely.
5. megaplan cloud bootstrap <idea-file> — upload idea file, then cloud exec to call megaplan init --idea-file --auto-start remotely.
6. megaplan cloud status --chain — fetch remote chain_state.json, invoke the core chain-status formatter on it. Do NOT reinvent the parser.

New providers:
7. Local provider (docker compose) — fastest iteration target, no Railway/cloud dependency. Becomes the CI-friendly smoke-test target.
8. SSH provider (plain docker-over-ssh) — 'any host with docker + ssh access' story.

Toolchain extensibility:
9. toolchains: block in cloud.yaml — declares one or more toolchains (rust, go, java, or custom with user-provided install snippet). Template renderer appends corresponding Dockerfile stages. Without this, the image is Python/Node only.

Hardening + retirement:
10. Secret redaction in cloud logs output (match known secret name patterns, replace with ***REDACTED***).
11. Clear error messages + documentation link when railway or docker CLI is missing at runtime.
12. ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ migration — deploy cloud with a cloud.yaml matching reigh's current env, run a tiny plan to verify parity, then delete the folder and replace with a MIGRATED.md pointer.

### Hard constraints
- Core commands MUST work locally without any cloud code loaded.
- Cloud wrappers MUST call out to core commands, not reimplement.
- Fly provider is OPTIONAL (skip if time-pressured).
- Preserve v0.19.0's public surface; this is additive.
- No breaking cloud.yaml changes from v0.19.0 (add fields, don't rename).
- Unit tests for every new core command; mocked-subprocess tests for every new provider; smoke test for local provider docker-compose lifecycle.

### Explicit non-goals
- No Kubernetes provider.
- No chain-of-chains.
- No cloud-specific chain status parser (the whole point of the core-first architecture).
- No version bump in this plan — sprint 2 ships as v0.20.0 but the bump + CHANGELOG commit is a separate follow-up.

### References
- Sprint 1 landed in v0.19.0 (2026-04-21). Full CHANGELOG entry in CHANGELOG.md.
- Reigh parity reference: ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ and megaplan/cloud/_reference/ (gitignored local copy of same).
- Verified launcher: ./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan (system python is 3.8, fails on NotRequired).
- Sprint 1 target retrospective: cloud subcommand CLI is already wired via megaplan/cloud/cli.py and dispatched from megaplan/cli.py.

Robustness: standard — feature-rich with architecture decisions to enforce, multiple independent pieces worth independent critique, gate useful for scope discipline.

    "Validation Order step 7 has a known text-level mismatch (accepted tradeoff): plan writes `cloud bootstrap` + `cloud status --chain` via marker as a single sequence, but `cloud bootstrap` never writes a marker. At manual-E2E time, split into two disjoint sequences: (a) `cloud chain <spec>` \u2192 `cloud status --chain` via marker \u2192 `cloud destroy`, and (b) `cloud bootstrap <idea>` \u2192 `cloud status` (non-chain default) \u2192 `cloud destroy`.",
    "Marker location MUST be provider-independent: `~/.megaplan/cloud/markers/<sha256(abs_path_of_cloud.yaml)[:16]>/last_chain.json`. Railway uses TemporaryDirectory; writing the marker inside the deploy dir would silently evaporate. T7's `_marker_dir(cloud_yaml_path)` helper is the ONLY place this path is derived \u2014 both T15 and T16 must call it; don't open-code the path.",
    "argv normalization MUST be the first line of `main()` in `megaplan/cli.py`. `cli_entry()` calls `main(argv=None)`; without `if argv is None: argv = sys.argv[1:]` at entry, the lazy `argv[0] == 'cloud'` intercept never fires for shell invocations. `tests/test_cli_entry.py` regression-guards this \u2014 do not delete it.",
    "Core/cloud isolation is a grep-enforced invariant. No `megaplan.cloud.*` import may appear in any core module. No cloud module may reimplement chain-state parsing beyond calling `chain.load_chain_state` / `chain.load_spec` / `chain.format_chain_status`. T20's grep check enforces this.",
    "Public `cloud.yaml` surface from v0.19.0 must parse unchanged \u2014 every v0.19.0 spec loads with no change in parsed `CloudSpec` fields. All additions (local/ssh blocks, toolchains) are additive with defaults.",
    "With `toolchains:` OMITTED, the rendered Dockerfile must be byte-identical to the v0.19.0 baseline. This is a byte-diff test, not a semantic-equivalence test \u2014 trailing newlines, whitespace, and comment order all count.",
    "`cloud bootstrap --plan-name` is OPTIONAL. When omitted, the remote command must NOT include `--name` \u2014 delegate to core's slug-based default. When set, include `--name {shlex.quote(args.plan_name)}`.",
    "Every interpolated value in SSH provider argv and `ssh_exec` call sites must pass through `shlex.quote`. This is a shell-injection surface; tests should assert quoting with adversarial inputs containing spaces, quotes, and `$`.",
    "LocalProvider and SshProvider should each stay under ~200 LOC (soft budget). If you're trending longer, look for patterns to push into the base class rather than expanding the concrete provider.",
    "`--session` is Railway-only. T8's `Provider.supports_session: bool` class attribute gates it. Do NOT hardcode `provider.name == \"railway\"` checks elsewhere in the CLI.",
    "The attach handler has a documented redaction gap (interactive pty precludes line-buffered wrapping). T17 requires this gap be noted in the attach handler's docstring so maintainers don't assume parity with `logs -f`.",
    "Fly provider stays deferred. `provider: fly` must raise a distinct 'future provider' error (not the same error as an unknown provider). Test this in `tests/test_cloud_spec.py`.",

        Idea:
Sprint 2 of the megaplan cloud feature — extend core megaplan ergonomics, add local + ssh providers, ship toolchain extensibility in cloud.yaml, retire the old reigh-megaplan-dev folder.

### Context
Sprint 1 shipped in v0.19.0 on 2026-04-21: built-in megaplan cloud subcommand (init/build/deploy/status/attach/logs/exec/resume/down/destroy) with a Railway provider, extracted from the ad-hoc setup at ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/. Spec schema lives in megaplan/cloud/spec.py, templates in megaplan/cloud/templates/, providers in megaplan/cloud/providers/.

Architectural principle established in sprint 1 and now codified: CORE megaplan owns capabilities, CLOUD subcommands are thin transport wrappers. Do not reinvent chain state parsing in cloud. Do not grow a parallel 'cloud chain *' surface. Core gets the command; cloud wraps it for remote execution.

### Sprint 2 deliverables

Core megaplan additions (must work locally without any cloud dependency):
1. megaplan chain start --spec <path> — validate spec, resolve referenced idea files, kick auto-loop per milestone. Replaces the 'init + auto' pair for chain runs.
2. megaplan chain status --spec <path> — read chain_state.json, pretty-print current_milestone, completed, remaining, per-milestone status. Unit tests against synthetic chain states.
3. megaplan init --idea-file <path> with optional --auto-start flag — read idea from a file instead of the positional CLI arg.

Cloud additions (thin wrappers over the new core commands):
4. megaplan cloud chain <spec.yaml> — upload spec, then cloud exec to call megaplan chain start remotely.
5. megaplan cloud bootstrap <idea-file> — upload idea file, then cloud exec to call megaplan init --idea-file --auto-start remotely.
6. megaplan cloud status --chain — fetch remote chain_state.json, invoke the core chain-status formatter on it. Do NOT reinvent the parser.

New providers:
7. Local provider (docker compose) — fastest iteration target, no Railway/cloud dependency. Becomes the CI-friendly smoke-test target.
8. SSH provider (plain docker-over-ssh) — 'any host with docker + ssh access' story.

Toolchain extensibility:
9. toolchains: block in cloud.yaml — declares one or more toolchains (rust, go, java, or custom with user-provided install snippet). Template renderer appends corresponding Dockerfile stages. Without this, the image is Python/Node only.

Hardening + retirement:
10. Secret redaction in cloud logs output (match known secret name patterns, replace with ***REDACTED***).
11. Clear error messages + documentation link when railway or docker CLI is missing at runtime.
12. ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ migration — deploy cloud with a cloud.yaml matching reigh's current env, run a tiny plan to verify parity, then delete the folder and replace with a MIGRATED.md pointer.

### Hard constraints
- Core commands MUST work locally without any cloud code loaded.
- Cloud wrappers MUST call out to core commands, not reimplement.
- Fly provider is OPTIONAL (skip if time-pressured).
- Preserve v0.19.0's public surface; this is additive.
- No breaking cloud.yaml changes from v0.19.0 (add fields, don't rename).
- Unit tests for every new core command; mocked-subprocess tests for every new provider; smoke test for local provider docker-compose lifecycle.

### Explicit non-goals
- No Kubernetes provider.
- No chain-of-chains.
- No cloud-specific chain status parser (the whole point of the core-first architecture).
- No version bump in this plan — sprint 2 ships as v0.20.0 but the bump + CHANGELOG commit is a separate follow-up.

### References
- Sprint 1 landed in v0.19.0 (2026-04-21). Full CHANGELOG entry in CHANGELOG.md.
- Reigh parity reference: ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ and megaplan/cloud/_reference/ (gitignored local copy of same).
- Verified launcher: ./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan (system python is 3.8, fails on NotRequired).
- Sprint 1 target retrospective: cloud subcommand CLI is already wired via megaplan/cloud/cli.py and dispatched from megaplan/cli.py.

Robustness: standard — feature-rich with architecture decisions to enforce, multiple independent pieces worth independent critique, gate useful for scope discipline.

Core megaplan owns plan, auto, and chain behavior; cloud subcommands stage files, pick a transport, and run the core commands remotely.\n+\n+Examples below use `megaplan ...`; in this repo run `./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan ...`. Add `--cloud-yaml /path/to/cloud.yaml` when `cloud.yaml` is not at the project root.\n+\n+## Providers\n+\n+| Provider | Use case | Notes |\n+|---|---|---|\n+| `railway` | Hosted runner with Railway SSH/logs/volume primitives | Good default for shared remote runs. |\n+| `local` | Fast local iteration and CI-friendly smoke tests | Uses `docker compose` from a persistent deploy dir under `~/.megaplan/cloud/<compose_project>/`. |\n+| `ssh` | Any reachable Docker host over SSH | Syncs the deploy dir to `ssh.remote_dir` with `rsync`, or `scp -r` when `rsync` is unavailable. |\n+\n+`provider: fly` remains reserved for a future release.\n+\n+## Quick Start\n+\n+1. Scaffold:\n+\n+```bash\n+megaplan cloud init\n+```\n+\n+2. Edit `cloud.yaml` for repo, provider, mode, secrets, and optional toolchains.\n+\n+3. Export the local secrets named under `secrets:`:\n+\n+```bash\n+export OPENAI_API_KEY=...\n+export GITHUB_TOKEN=...        # optional, but recommended for push/private clone\n+export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...   # optional\n+```\n+\n+4. Build and deploy:\n+\n+```bash\n+megaplan cloud build\n+megaplan cloud deploy\n+```\n+\n+5. Start work remotely:\n+\n+```bash\n+megaplan cloud bootstrap ideas/tiny-plan.txt\n+megaplan cloud chain chain.yaml --idea-dir ideas\n+```\n+\n+6. Inspect and connect:\n+\n+```bash\n+megaplan cloud status\n+megaplan cloud status --chain\n+megaplan cloud logs\n+megaplan cloud attach\n+```\n+\n+## `cloud.yaml` Reference\n+\n+### Top-level fields\n+\n+| Field | Required | Default | Meaning |\n+|---|---|---:|---|\n+| `provider` | no | `railway` | One of `railway`, `local`, or `ssh`. |\n+| `mode` | no | `idle` | Runner mode: `auto`, `chain`, or `idle`. |\n+| `secrets` | no | `[]` | Local env var names uploaded during `megaplan cloud deploy` and redacted from cloud log output where possible. |\n+| `toolchains` | no | `[]` | Extra language toolchains layered into the image. Use aliases `rust`, `go`, `java`, or `{name, install}` mappings. |\n+\n+### `repo`\n+\n+| Field | Required | Default | Meaning |\n+|---|---|---:|---|\n+| `repo.url` | yes | none | Git URL cloned into the remote workspace. |\n+| `repo.branch` | no | `main` | Branch checked out on clone. |\n+| `repo.workspace` | no | `/workspace/app` | Absolute repo path used for remote `cd`, tmux, file uploads, and wrapper commands. |\n+\n+### `agents`\n+\n+| Field | Required | Default | Meaning |\n+|---|---|---:|---|\n+| `agents.default` | no | `codex` | Default megaplan agent for routed steps. |\n+| `agents.<step>` | no | inherits `default` | Optional per-step override such as `plan`, `review`, `execute`, or `loop_execute`. |\n+\n+### `codex`\n+\n+| Field | Required | Default | Meaning |\n+|---|---|---:|---|\n+| `codex.model` | no | `gpt-5.4` | Written into `/root/.codex/config.toml` on boot. |\n+| `codex.reasoning` | no | `high` | Reasoning level written into `/root/.codex/config.toml` on boot. |\n+\n+### `auto`\n+\n+Used only when `mode: auto`.\n+\n+| Field | Required in `auto` mode | Default | Meaning |\n+|---|---|---:|---|\n+| `auto.plan_name` | yes | none | Remote plan name for boot-time `megaplan auto --plan ...`. |\n+| `auto.idea_file` | yes | none | Absolute remote path to the idea file already staged on the workspace volume. |\n+| `auto.robustness` | no | `standard` | Robustness for the boot-time init fallback. |\n+\n+### `chain`\n+\n+Used only when `mode: chain`.\n+\n+| Field | Required in `chain` mode | Default | Meaning |\n+|---|---|---:|---|\n+| `chain.spec` | yes | none | Absolute remote path to the already-staged chain spec. |\n+\n+### `megaplan`\n+\n+| Field | Required | Default | Meaning |\n+|---|---|---:|---|\n+| `megaplan.ref` | no | `main` | Branch, tag, or SHA installed on boot via `pip install --upgrade git+...@<ref>`. |\n+\n+### `resources`\n+\n+| Field | Required | Default | Meaning |\n+|---|---|---:|---|\n+| `resources.volume` | no | none | Provider-specific persistent volume name. `destroy` deletes it only when set. |\n+| `resources.port` | no | `8080` | Health server port exposed by the container. |\n+\n+### `railway`\n+\n+| Field | Required | Default | Meaning |\n+|---|---|---:|---|\n+| `railway.service` | no | `agent` | Railway service name used by `deploy`, `logs`, and `down`. |\n+| `railway.session` | no | `agent` | Railway SSH session name used for interactive attaches. |\n+| `railway.project` | no | unset | Optional project passed to `railway link --project ...` before deploy. |\n+\n+### `local`\n+\n+| Field | Required when `provider: local` | Default | Meaning |\n+|---|---|---:|---|\n+| `local.compose_project` | no | `megaplan-cloud` | Docker Compose project name used for build, logs, exec, and teardown. |\n+| `local.workdir` | no | `workspace` | Bind-mounted directory inside the persistent local deploy dir. |\n+\n+### `ssh`\n+\n+| Field | Required when `provider: ssh` | Default | Meaning |\n+|---|---|---:|---|\n+| `ssh.host` | yes | none | Remote SSH host. |\n+| `ssh.user` | no | unset | Optional SSH username. |\n+| `ssh.port` | no | `22` | SSH port. |\n+| `ssh.identity_file` | no | unset | Optional identity file passed to `ssh`, `scp`, and `rsync`. |\n+| `ssh.remote_dir` | no | `/tmp/megaplan-cloud` | Remote directory used for synced Docker build context and `.env`. |\n+| `ssh.container` | no | `megaplan-cloud-agent` | Remote container name and image tag. |\n+\n+## Toolchains\n+\n+Without `toolchains:`, the image is Python/Node only. Add built-in aliases or a custom install snippet:\n+\n+```yaml\n+toolchains:\n+  - rust\n+  - go\n+  - name: custom\n+    install: |\n+      RUN curl -fsSL https://example.com/tool/install.sh | bash\n+```\n+\n+## Wrapper Workflows\n+\n+### `megaplan cloud bootstrap <idea-file>`\n+\n+`cloud bootstrap` uploads a local idea file to `<repo.workspace>/idea.txt`, then runs:\n+\n+```bash\n+megaplan init --project-dir <workspace> --idea-file <workspace>/idea.txt --auto-start --robustness <level>\n+```\n+\n+`--plan-name` is optional. If omitted, cloud does **not** pass `--name`; core megaplan chooses the default slug from the idea text.\n+\n+### `megaplan cloud chain <spec> [--idea-dir <dir>]`\n+\n+`cloud chain` is the preferred path for remote chain runs. It:\n+\n+1. Parses the local chain spec with core `megaplan.chain.load_spec(...)`.\n+2. Resolves each milestone idea file from `--idea-dir` or, by default, the local spec's parent directory.\n+3. Uploads each idea file to the remote path named in the chain spec.\n+4. Uploads the chain spec to `<repo.workspace>/chain.yaml`.\n+5. Runs remote `megaplan chain start --spec <repo.workspace>/chain.yaml`.\n+\n+After upload + dispatch, cloud writes a provider-independent marker:\n+\n+```text\n+~/.megaplan/cloud/markers/<sha256(abs_path_of_cloud.yaml)[:16]>/last_chain.json\n+```\n+\n+That marker survives Railway's ephemeral deploy dir and is used by `cloud status --chain`.\n+\n+### `megaplan cloud status --chain`\n+\n+`cloud status --chain` fetches remote `chain_state.json`, then reuses core chain status formatting. Remote spec resolution precedence is:\n+\n+1. `--remote-spec <path>`\n+2. `~/.megaplan/cloud/markers/<sha>/last_chain.json`\n+3. `spec.chain.spec` from `cloud.yaml` when `mode: chain`\n+4. Otherwise `missing_remote_spec`\n+\n+The command prints the structured payload on stdout and the same human-readable chain summary block that local `megaplan chain status --spec ...` prints on stderr.\n+\n+### `megaplan cloud status`\n+\n+Without `--chain`, `cloud status` still runs remote `megaplan status` and prints that JSON payload unchanged.\n+\n+## Boot-Time Runner Modes\n+\n+`mode: auto` and `mode: chain` still control what the long-running remote `agent` session launches on boot. Those boot paths expect the referenced remote files to already exist on the workspace volume.\n+\n+Use `cloud bootstrap` and `cloud chain` when you want cloud to stage the local input files for you. If you set `mode: auto` or `mode: chain` directly in `cloud.yaml`, make sure the referenced remote files already exist before restart.\n+\n+## Logs, Redaction, And Attach\n+\n+`megaplan cloud logs` redacts:\n+\n+- literal values for secret names listed under `secrets:` when those values are present locally\n+- `NAME=value` and `NAME: value` patterns for those secret names\n+- known token shapes such as `sk-...`, `ghp_...`, and `xoxb-...`\n+\n+This redaction applies to:\n+\n+- `megaplan cloud logs`\n+- `megaplan cloud exec`\n+- wrapper-dispatched output from `cloud bootstrap`, `cloud chain`, and `cloud resume`\n+\n+`megaplan cloud attach` is different. It opens a raw interactive PTY, so line-buffered redaction is not applied there. Treat attach sessions as trusted terminals.\n+\n+## Provider Notes\n+\n+### `provider: local`\n+\n+- Uses `docker compose -p <compose_project> -f ~/.megaplan/cloud/<compose_project>/docker-compose.yaml ...`\n+- Materializes a persistent deploy dir under `~/.megaplan/cloud/<compose_project>/`\n+- Bind-mounts `./<local.workdir>` into `<repo.workspace>`\n+- Best for local iteration and CI smoke tests\n+\n+### `provider: ssh`\n+\n+- Uses plain `ssh` for exec/logs/attach/status\n+- Syncs the materialized deploy dir to `ssh.remote_dir`\n+- Prefers `rsync`; falls back to `scp -r` with a warning when `rsync` is unavailable\n+- Runs a single long-lived Docker container named `ssh.container`\n+\n+### `provider: railway`\n+\n+- Uses Railway SSH/logs/down/volume primitives\n+- Markers are stored outside the Railway deploy dir so chain status survives redeploys\n+- `--session` remains Railway-only\n+\n+## Runtime Requirements\n+\n+- Railway CLI install docs: https://docs.railway.app/develop/cli\n+- Docker install docs: https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/\n+- OpenSSH project/docs: https://www.openssh.com/\n+\n+## Migration From `reigh-megaplan-dev`\n+\n+Use the human-executed runbook at [docs/cloud-migration-from-reigh.md](cloud-migration-from-reigh.md). The important rule is: write `MIGRATED.md` first, then remove siblings while preserving that pointer file.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

        Idea:
Sprint 2 of the megaplan cloud feature — extend core megaplan ergonomics, add local + ssh providers, ship toolchain extensibility in cloud.yaml, retire the old reigh-megaplan-dev folder.

### Context
Sprint 1 shipped in v0.19.0 on 2026-04-21: built-in megaplan cloud subcommand (init/build/deploy/status/attach/logs/exec/resume/down/destroy) with a Railway provider, extracted from the ad-hoc setup at ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/. Spec schema lives in megaplan/cloud/spec.py, templates in megaplan/cloud/templates/, providers in megaplan/cloud/providers/.

Architectural principle established in sprint 1 and now codified: CORE megaplan owns capabilities, CLOUD subcommands are thin transport wrappers. Do not reinvent chain state parsing in cloud. Do not grow a parallel 'cloud chain *' surface. Core gets the command; cloud wraps it for remote execution.

### Sprint 2 deliverables

Core megaplan additions (must work locally without any cloud dependency):
1. megaplan chain start --spec <path> — validate spec, resolve referenced idea files, kick auto-loop per milestone. Replaces the 'init + auto' pair for chain runs.
2. megaplan chain status --spec <path> — read chain_state.json, pretty-print current_milestone, completed, remaining, per-milestone status. Unit tests against synthetic chain states.
3. megaplan init --idea-file <path> with optional --auto-start flag — read idea from a file instead of the positional CLI arg.

Cloud additions (thin wrappers over the new core commands):
4. megaplan cloud chain <spec.yaml> — upload spec, then cloud exec to call megaplan chain start remotely.
5. megaplan cloud bootstrap <idea-file> — upload idea file, then cloud exec to call megaplan init --idea-file --auto-start remotely.
6. megaplan cloud status --chain — fetch remote chain_state.json, invoke the core chain-status formatter on it. Do NOT reinvent the parser.

New providers:
7. Local provider (docker compose) — fastest iteration target, no Railway/cloud dependency. Becomes the CI-friendly smoke-test target.
8. SSH provider (plain docker-over-ssh) — 'any host with docker + ssh access' story.

Toolchain extensibility:
9. toolchains: block in cloud.yaml — declares one or more toolchains (rust, go, java, or custom with user-provided install snippet). Template renderer appends corresponding Dockerfile stages. Without this, the image is Python/Node only.

Hardening + retirement:
10. Secret redaction in cloud logs output (match known secret name patterns, replace with ***REDACTED***).
11. Clear error messages + documentation link when railway or docker CLI is missing at runtime.
12. ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ migration — deploy cloud with a cloud.yaml matching reigh's current env, run a tiny plan to verify parity, then delete the folder and replace with a MIGRATED.md pointer.

### Hard constraints
- Core commands MUST work locally without any cloud code loaded.
- Cloud wrappers MUST call out to core commands, not reimplement.
- Fly provider is OPTIONAL (skip if time-pressured).
- Preserve v0.19.0's public surface; this is additive.
- No breaking cloud.yaml changes from v0.19.0 (add fields, don't rename).
- Unit tests for every new core command; mocked-subprocess tests for every new provider; smoke test for local provider docker-compose lifecycle.

### Explicit non-goals
- No Kubernetes provider.
- No chain-of-chains.
- No cloud-specific chain status parser (the whole point of the core-first architecture).
- No version bump in this plan — sprint 2 ships as v0.20.0 but the bump + CHANGELOG commit is a separate follow-up.

### References
- Sprint 1 landed in v0.19.0 (2026-04-21). Full CHANGELOG entry in CHANGELOG.md.
- Reigh parity reference: ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ and megaplan/cloud/_reference/ (gitignored local copy of same).
- Verified launcher: ./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan (system python is 3.8, fails on NotRequired).
- Sprint 1 target retrospective: cloud subcommand CLI is already wired via megaplan/cloud/cli.py and dispatched from megaplan/cli.py.

Robustness: standard — feature-rich with architecture decisions to enforce, multiple independent pieces worth independent critique, gate useful for scope discipline.

    "Validation Order step 7 has a known text-level mismatch (accepted tradeoff): plan writes `cloud bootstrap` + `cloud status --chain` via marker as a single sequence, but `cloud bootstrap` never writes a marker.     "Marker location MUST be provider-independent: `~/.megaplan/cloud/markers/<sha256(abs_path_of_cloud.yaml)[:16]>/last_chain.json`. Railway uses TemporaryDirectory; writing the marker inside the deploy dir would silently evaporate. T7's `_marker_dir(cloud_yaml_path)` helper is the ONLY place this path is derived \u2014 both T15 and T16 must call it; don't open-code the path.",
    "argv normalization MUST be the first line of `main()` in `megaplan/cli.py`. `cli_entry()` calls `main(argv=None)`; without `if argv is None: argv = sys.argv[1:]` at entry, the lazy `argv[0] == 'cloud'` intercept never fires for shell invocations. `tests/test_cli_entry.py` regression-guards this \u2014 do not delete it.",
    "Core/cloud isolation is a grep-enforced invariant. No `megaplan.cloud.*` import may appear in any core module. No cloud module may reimplement chain-state parsing beyond calling `chain.load_chain_state` / `chain.load_spec` / `chain.format_chain_status`. T20's grep check enforces this.",
    "Public `cloud.yaml` surface from v0.19.0 must parse unchanged \u2014 every v0.19.0 spec loads with no change in parsed `CloudSpec` fields. All additions (local/ssh blocks, toolchains) are additive with defaults.",
    "With `toolchains:` OMITTED, the rendered Dockerfile must be byte-identical to the v0.19.0 baseline. This is a byte-diff test, not a semantic-equivalence test \u2014 trailing newlines, whitespace, and comment order all count.",
    "`cloud bootstrap --plan-name` is OPTIONAL. When omitted, the remote command must NOT include `--name` \u2014 delegate to core's slug-based default. When set, include `--name {shlex.quote(args.plan_name)}`.",
    "Every interpolated value in SSH provider argv and `ssh_exec` call sites must pass through `shlex.quote`. This is a shell-injection surface; tests should assert quoting with adversarial inputs containing spaces, quotes, and `$`.",
    "LocalProvider and SshProvider should each stay under ~200 LOC (soft budget). If you're trending longer, look for patterns to push into the base class rather than expanding the concrete provider.",
    "`--session` is Railway-only. T8's `Provider.supports_session: bool` class attribute gates it. Do NOT hardcode `provider.name == \"railway\"` checks elsewhere in the CLI.",
    "The attach handler has a documented redaction gap (interactive pty precludes line-buffered wrapping). T17 requires this gap be noted in the attach handler's docstring so maintainers don't assume parity with `logs -f`.",
    "Fly provider stays deferred. `provider: fly` must raise a distinct 'future provider' error (not the same error as an unknown provider). Test this in `tests/test_cloud_spec.py`.",

label: m1\n+                    idea: {idea_path}\n+                \"\"\"\n+            ),\n+            encoding=\"utf-8\",\n+        )\n+\n+        state_path = tmp_path / \"chain_state.json\"\n+        state_path.write_text(\n+            json.dumps(\n+                {\n+                    \"current_milestone_index\": 0,\n+                    \"current_plan_name\": \"chain-plan\",\n+                    \"last_state\": \"done\",\n+                    \"completed\": [],\n+                }\n+            ),\n+            encoding=\"utf-8\",\n+        )\n+\n+        sys.modules[\"megaplan.cloud\"] = None\n+        sys.modules.pop(\"megaplan.cloud.cli\", None)\n+\n+        import megaplan.cli as cli\n+\n+        stdout = io.StringIO()\n+        stderr = io.StringIO()\n+        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(stdout), contextlib.redirect_stderr(stderr):\n+            exit_code = cli.main([\"chain\", \"status\", \"--spec\", str(spec_path)])\n+\n+        payload = {\n+            \"exit_code\": exit_code,\n+            \"cloud_modules\": sorted(\n+                name\n+                for name, module in sys.modules.items()\n+                if name.startswith(\"megaplan.cloud\") and module is not None\n+            ),\n+            \"stdout\": json.loads(stdout.getvalue()),\n+            \"stderr\": stderr.getvalue().splitlines(),\n+        }\n+        print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True))\n+    return 0\n+\n+\n+if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n+    raise SystemExit(main())\n*** End Patch\n"

        Idea:
Sprint 2 of the megaplan cloud feature — extend core megaplan ergonomics, add local + ssh providers, ship toolchain extensibility in cloud.yaml, retire the old reigh-megaplan-dev folder.

### Context
Sprint 1 shipped in v0.19.0 on 2026-04-21: built-in megaplan cloud subcommand (init/build/deploy/status/attach/logs/exec/resume/down/destroy) with a Railway provider, extracted from the ad-hoc setup at ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/. Spec schema lives in megaplan/cloud/spec.py, templates in megaplan/cloud/templates/, providers in megaplan/cloud/providers/.

Architectural principle established in sprint 1 and now codified: CORE megaplan owns capabilities, CLOUD subcommands are thin transport wrappers. Do not reinvent chain state parsing in cloud. Do not grow a parallel 'cloud chain *' surface. Core gets the command; cloud wraps it for remote execution.

### Sprint 2 deliverables

Core megaplan additions (must work locally without any cloud dependency):
1. megaplan chain start --spec <path> — validate spec, resolve referenced idea files, kick auto-loop per milestone. Replaces the 'init + auto' pair for chain runs.
2. megaplan chain status --spec <path> — read chain_state.json, pretty-print current_milestone, completed, remaining, per-milestone status. Unit tests against synthetic chain states.
3. megaplan init --idea-file <path> with optional --auto-start flag — read idea from a file instead of the positional CLI arg.

Cloud additions (thin wrappers over the new core commands):
4. megaplan cloud chain <spec.yaml> — upload spec, then cloud exec to call megaplan chain start remotely.
5. megaplan cloud bootstrap <idea-file> — upload idea file, then cloud exec to call megaplan init --idea-file --auto-start remotely.
6. megaplan cloud status --chain — fetch remote chain_state.json, invoke the core chain-status formatter on it. Do NOT reinvent the parser.

New providers:
7. Local provider (docker compose) — fastest iteration target, no Railway/cloud dependency. Becomes the CI-friendly smoke-test target.
8. SSH provider (plain docker-over-ssh) — 'any host with docker + ssh access' story.

Toolchain extensibility:
9. toolchains: block in cloud.yaml — declares one or more toolchains (rust, go, java, or custom with user-provided install snippet). Template renderer appends corresponding Dockerfile stages. Without this, the image is Python/Node only.

Hardening + retirement:
10. Secret redaction in cloud logs output (match known secret name patterns, replace with ***REDACTED***).
11. Clear error messages + documentation link when railway or docker CLI is missing at runtime.
12. ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ migration — deploy cloud with a cloud.yaml matching reigh's current env, run a tiny plan to verify parity, then delete the folder and replace with a MIGRATED.md pointer.

### Hard constraints
- Core commands MUST work locally without any cloud code loaded.
- Cloud wrappers MUST call out to core commands, not reimplement.
- Fly provider is OPTIONAL (skip if time-pressured).
- Preserve v0.19.0's public surface; this is additive.
- No breaking cloud.yaml changes from v0.19.0 (add fields, don't rename).
- Unit tests for every new core command; mocked-subprocess tests for every new provider; smoke test for local provider docker-compose lifecycle.

### Explicit non-goals
- No Kubernetes provider.
- No chain-of-chains.
- No cloud-specific chain status parser (the whole point of the core-first architecture).
- No version bump in this plan — sprint 2 ships as v0.20.0 but the bump + CHANGELOG commit is a separate follow-up.

- Sprint 1 target retrospective: cloud subcommand CLI is already wired via megaplan/cloud/cli.py and dispatched from megaplan/cli.py.

Robustness: standard — feature-rich with architecture decisions to enforce, multiple independent pieces worth independent critique, gate useful for scope discipline.

    "idea": "Sprint 2 of the megaplan cloud feature \u2014 extend core megaplan ergonomics, add local + ssh providers, ship toolchain extensibility in cloud.yaml, retire the old reigh-megaplan-dev folder.\n\n### Context\nSprint 1 shipped in v0.19.0 on 2026-04-21: built-in megaplan cloud subcommand (init/build/deploy/status/attach/logs/exec/resume/down/destroy) with a Railway provider, extracted from the ad-hoc setup at ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/. Spec schema lives in megaplan/cloud/spec.py, templates in megaplan/cloud/templates/, providers in megaplan/cloud/providers/.\n\nArchitectural principle established in sprint 1 and now codified: CORE megaplan owns capabilities, CLOUD subcommands are thin transport wrappers. Do not reinvent chain state parsing in cloud. Do not grow a parallel 'cloud chain *' surface. Core gets the command; cloud wraps it for remote execution.\n\n### Sprint 2 deliverables\n\nCore megaplan additions (must work locally without any cloud dependency):\n1. megaplan chain start --spec <path> \u2014 validate spec, resolve referenced idea files, kick auto-loop per milestone. Replaces the 'init + auto' pair for chain runs.\n2. megaplan chain status --spec <path> \u2014 read chain_state.json, pretty-print current_milestone, completed, remaining, per-milestone status. Unit tests against synthetic chain states.\n3. megaplan init --idea-file <path> with optional --auto-start flag \u2014 read idea from a file instead of the positional CLI arg.\n\nCloud additions (thin wrappers over the new core commands):\n4. megaplan cloud chain <spec.yaml> \u2014 upload spec, then cloud exec to call megaplan chain start remotely.\n5. megaplan cloud bootstrap <idea-file> \u2014 upload idea file, then cloud exec to call megaplan init --idea-file --auto-start remotely.\n6. megaplan cloud status --chain \u2014 fetch remote chain_state.json, invoke the core chain-status formatter on it. Do NOT reinvent the parser.\n\nNew providers:\n7. Local provider (docker compose) \u2014 fastest iteration target, no Railway/cloud dependency. Becomes the CI-friendly smoke-test target.\n8. SSH provider (plain docker-over-ssh) \u2014 'any host with docker + ssh access' story.\n\nToolchain extensibility:\n9. toolchains: block in cloud.yaml \u2014 declares one or more toolchains (rust, go, java, or custom with user-provided install snippet). Template renderer appends corresponding Dockerfile stages. Without this, the image is Python/Node only.\n\nHardening + retirement:\n10. Secret redaction in cloud logs output (match known secret name patterns, replace with ***REDACTED***).\n11. Clear error messages + documentation link when railway or docker CLI is missing at runtime.\n12. ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ migration \u2014 deploy cloud with a cloud.yaml matching reigh's current env, run a tiny plan to verify parity, then delete the folder and replace with a MIGRATED.md pointer.\n\n### Hard constraints\n- Core commands MUST work locally without any cloud code loaded.\n- Cloud wrappers MUST call out to core commands, not reimplement.\n- Fly provider is OPTIONAL (skip if time-pressured).\n- Preserve v0.19.0's public surface; this is additive.\n- No breaking cloud.yaml changes from v0.19.0 (add fields, don't rename).\n- Unit tests for every new core command; mocked-subprocess tests for every new provider; smoke test for local provider docker-compose lifecycle.\n\n### Explicit non-goals\n- No Kubernetes provider.\n- No chain-of-chains.\n- No cloud-specific chain status parser (the whole point of the core-first architecture).\n- No version bump in this plan \u2014 sprint 2 ships as v0.20.0 but the bump + CHANGELOG commit is a separate follow-up.\n\n### References\n- Sprint 1 landed in v0.19.0 (2026-04-21). Full CHANGELOG entry in CHANGELOG.md.\n- Reigh parity reference: ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ and megaplan/cloud/_reference/ (gitignored local copy of same).\n- Verified launcher: ./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan (system python is 3.8, fails on NotRequired).\n- Sprint 1 target retrospective: cloud subcommand CLI is already wired via megaplan/cloud/cli.py and dispatched from megaplan/cli.py.\n\nRobustness: standard \u2014 feature-rich with architecture decisions to enforce, multiple independent pieces worth independent critique, gate useful for scope discipline.",

        "resolution": "Two surgical one-liners per gate v3 guidance \u2014 no structural change. This decouples the marker from the deploy dir, so Railway's `TemporaryDirectory` flow no longer loses the ad-hoc chain reference between `cloud chain` and `cloud status --chain`. Step 16's precedence now reads from `_marker_dir(...)`, not the deploy dir. Gate's recommended key derivation (SHA of `cloud.yaml` absolute path) adopted verbatim to match the \"one deploy dir per cloud.yaml\" mental model. Everything else from Rev 3 is verbatim. Watch items to keep visible during execution:
- Validation Order step 7 has a known text-level mismatch (accepted tradeoff): plan writes `cloud bootstrap` + `cloud status --chain` via marker as a single sequence, but `cloud bootstrap` never writes a marker. At manual-E2E time, split into two disjoint sequences: (a) `cloud chain <spec>` → `cloud status --chain` via marker → `cloud destroy`, and (b) `cloud bootstrap <idea>` → `cloud status` (non-chain default) → `cloud destroy`.
- Marker location MUST be provider-independent: `~/.megaplan/cloud/markers/<sha256(abs_path_of_cloud.yaml)[:16]>/last_chain.json`. Railway uses TemporaryDirectory; writing the marker inside the deploy dir would silently evaporate. T7's `_marker_dir(cloud_yaml_path)` helper is the ONLY place this path is derived — both T15 and T16 must call it; don't open-code the path.
- argv normalization MUST be the first line of `main()` in `megaplan/cli.py`. `cli_entry()` calls `main(argv=None)`; without `if argv is None: argv = sys.argv[1:]` at entry, the lazy `argv[0] == 'cloud'` intercept never fires for shell invocations. `tests/test_cli_entry.py` regression-guards this — do not delete it.
- Core/cloud isolation is a grep-enforced invariant. No `megaplan.cloud.*` import may appear in any core module. No cloud module may reimplement chain-state parsing beyond calling `chain.load_chain_state` / `chain.load_spec` / `chain.format_chain_status`. T20's grep check enforces this.
- Public `cloud.yaml` surface from v0.19.0 must parse unchanged — every v0.19.0 spec loads with no change in parsed `CloudSpec` fields. All additions (local/ssh blocks, toolchains) are additive with defaults.
- With `toolchains:` OMITTED, the rendered Dockerfile must be byte-identical to the v0.19.0 baseline. This is a byte-diff test, not a semantic-equivalence test — trailing newlines, whitespace, and comment order all count.
- `cloud bootstrap --plan-name` is OPTIONAL. When omitted, the remote command must NOT include `--name` — delegate to core's slug-based default. When set, include `--name {shlex.quote(args.plan_name)}`.
- Every interpolated value in SSH provider argv and `ssh_exec` call sites must pass through `shlex.quote`. This is a shell-injection surface; tests should assert quoting with adversarial inputs containing spaces, quotes, and `$`.
- LocalProvider and SshProvider should each stay under ~200 LOC (soft budget). If you're trending longer, look for patterns to push into the base class rather than expanding the concrete provider.
- `--session` is Railway-only. T8's `Provider.supports_session: bool` class attribute gates it. Do NOT hardcode `provider.name == "railway"` checks elsewhere in the CLI.
- The attach handler has a documented redaction gap (interactive pty precludes line-buffered wrapping). T17 requires this gap be noted in the attach handler's docstring so maintainers don't assume parity with `logs -f`.
- Fly provider stays deferred. `provider: fly` must raise a distinct 'future provider' error (not the same error as an unknown provider). Test this in `tests/test_cloud_spec.py`.
- Reigh folder deletion is HUMAN-EXECUTED. T19 only drafts the runbook; do not auto-execute `rm -rf` against `~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/`. The safe ordering is: write `MIGRATED.md` FIRST, then `find -mindepth 1 ! -name MIGRATED.md -print0 | xargs -0 rm -rf` to preserve the pointer.
- Use `./.venv/bin/python -m pytest` and `./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan` throughout. System Python (3.8) fails on `NotRequired` imports.
- Assumption #3 from the plan: `--auto-start` on `megaplan init` runs `auto.drive()` IN-PROCESS and blocks until terminal. T3 must call `megaplan.auto.drive(plan_name, cwd=root, ...)` directly, not via subprocess.

        Idea:
Sprint 2 of the megaplan cloud feature — extend core megaplan ergonomics, add local + ssh providers, ship toolchain extensibility in cloud.yaml, retire the old reigh-megaplan-dev folder.

### Context
Sprint 1 shipped in v0.19.0 on 2026-04-21: built-in megaplan cloud subcommand (init/build/deploy/status/attach/logs/exec/resume/down/destroy) with a Railway provider, extracted from the ad-hoc setup at ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/. Spec schema lives in megaplan/cloud/spec.py, templates in megaplan/cloud/templates/, providers in megaplan/cloud/providers/.

Architectural principle established in sprint 1 and now codified: CORE megaplan owns capabilities, CLOUD subcommands are thin transport wrappers. Do not reinvent chain state parsing in cloud. Do not grow a parallel 'cloud chain *' surface. Core gets the command; cloud wraps it for remote execution.

### Sprint 2 deliverables

Core megaplan additions (must work locally without any cloud dependency):
1. megaplan chain start --spec <path> — validate spec, resolve referenced idea files, kick auto-loop per milestone. Replaces the 'init + auto' pair for chain runs.
2. megaplan chain status --spec <path> — read chain_state.json, pretty-print current_milestone, completed, remaining, per-milestone status. Unit tests against synthetic chain states.
3. megaplan init --idea-file <path> with optional --auto-start flag — read idea from a file instead of the positional CLI arg.

Cloud additions (thin wrappers over the new core commands):
4. megaplan cloud chain <spec.yaml> — upload spec, then cloud exec to call megaplan chain start remotely.
5. megaplan cloud bootstrap <idea-file> — upload idea file, then cloud exec to call megaplan init --idea-file --auto-start remotely.
6. megaplan cloud status --chain — fetch remote chain_state.json, invoke the core chain-status formatter on it. Do NOT reinvent the parser.

New providers:
7. Local provider (docker compose) — fastest iteration target, no Railway/cloud dependency. Becomes the CI-friendly smoke-test target.
8. SSH provider (plain docker-over-ssh) — 'any host with docker + ssh access' story.

Toolchain extensibility:
9. toolchains: block in cloud.yaml — declares one or more toolchains (rust, go, java, or custom with user-provided install snippet). Template renderer appends corresponding Dockerfile stages. Without this, the image is Python/Node only.

Hardening + retirement:
10. Secret redaction in cloud logs output (match known secret name patterns, replace with ***REDACTED***).
11. Clear error messages + documentation link when railway or docker CLI is missing at runtime.
12. ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ migration — deploy cloud with a cloud.yaml matching reigh's current env, run a tiny plan to verify parity, then delete the folder and replace with a MIGRATED.md pointer.

### Hard constraints
- Core commands MUST work locally without any cloud code loaded.
- Cloud wrappers MUST call out to core commands, not reimplement.
- Fly provider is OPTIONAL (skip if time-pressured).
- Preserve v0.19.0's public surface; this is additive.
- No breaking cloud.yaml changes from v0.19.0 (add fields, don't rename).
- Unit tests for every new core command; mocked-subprocess tests for every new provider; smoke test for local provider docker-compose lifecycle.

### Explicit non-goals
- No Kubernetes provider.
- No chain-of-chains.
- No cloud-specific chain status parser (the whole point of the core-first architecture).
- No version bump in this plan — sprint 2 ships as v0.20.0 but the bump + CHANGELOG commit is a separate follow-up.

### References
- Sprint 1 landed in v0.19.0 (2026-04-21). Full CHANGELOG entry in CHANGELOG.md.
- Reigh parity reference: ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ and megaplan/cloud/_reference/ (gitignored local copy of same).
- Verified launcher: ./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan (system python is 3.8, fails on NotRequired).
- Sprint 1 target retrospective: cloud subcommand CLI is already wired via megaplan/cloud/cli.py and dispatched from megaplan/cli.py.

Robustness: standard — feature-rich with architecture decisions to enforce, multiple independent pieces worth independent critique, gate useful for scope discipline.

      "rationale": "Matches chain's blocking model."
    },
    {
      "id": "SD-006",
      "decision": "Local and SSH providers use persistent per-project deploy directories under `~/.megaplan/cloud/<proj>/`; Railway keeps TemporaryDirectory.",
      "rationale": "Docker-compose lifecycle requires persistence across build/exec/down; Railway is stateless."
    },
    {
      "id": "SD-007",
      "decision": "Follow-mode `logs -f` redaction via line-buffered `stream_redact(Popen)`; `attach` is a documented gap.",
      "rationale": "Closes the default-path redaction hole; pty interactivity precludes line-wrapping attach."
    },
    {
      "id": "SD-008",
      "decision": "`--session` gated via `Provider.supports_session: bool`; Railway True, Local/SSH False.",
      "rationale": "Provider-opt-in pattern replaces Railway-hardcoded check."
    },
    {
      "id": "SD-009",
      "decision": "Parser isolation via `_register_cloud_subcommands(parser)` + thin `build_cloud_parser(subparsers)` wrapper; `main()` normalizes `argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv` before the lazy intercept keys on `argv[0] == 'cloud'`.",
      "rationale": "Clean split between API shape and subcommand registration; works for both `main([...])` test invocations and `cli_entry()` shell invocations."
    },
    {
      "id": "SD-010",
      "decision": "Subprocess launchers in `auto.py`/`chain.py` use `[sys.executable, '-m', 'megaplan', ...]`; in-container wrappers keep bare `megaplan`.",
      "rationale": "Matches the brief's verified launcher."
    },
    {
      "id": "SD-011",
      "decision": "`cloud chain` path contract: spec paths treated as remote; local sources resolved by stripping `spec.repo.workspace` prefix and looking under `--idea-dir` (default: spec's parent).",
      "rationale": "Matches bundled `chain.yaml.example` + `docs/cloud.md` conventions."
    },

      "id": "SD-012",

    },

      "id": "SD-013",
      "decision": "Reigh retirement runbook writes `MIGRATED.md` first, then `find -mindepth 1 ! -name MIGRATED.md -delete` clears siblings while preserving pointer + parent dir.",
      "rationale": "Automation-safe ordering; resolved iter-2 rm-rf order bug."
    },

      "decision": "Documentation scope explicitly includes `docs/cloud.md` (authoritative cloud reference per `README.md:108-113`) alongside `README.md` and `cloud.yaml.tmpl`; the marker location `~/.megaplan/cloud/markers/<sha>/last_chain.json` is documented so users can inspect state on disk.",
      "rationale": "Closes the scope/all_locations gap iter-2 raised."
    },
    {
      "id": "SD-015",
      "decision": "Manual E2E verification (Validation Order step 7) is split into two sequences at execution time: (a) `cloud chain <spec>` \u2192 `cloud status --chain` via marker \u2192 `cloud destroy`, (b) `cloud bootstrap <idea>` \u2192 `cloud status` (non-chain) \u2192 `cloud destroy`. Never mixed in a single sequence.",
      "rationale": "Resolves the iter-4 text-level mismatch in the validation section; the two wrappers have disjoint input/output contracts."

    "iteration": 4,
    "idea": "Sprint 2 of the megaplan cloud feature \u2014 extend core megaplan ergonomics, add local + ssh providers, ship toolchain extensibility in cloud.yaml, retire the old reigh-megaplan-dev folder.\n\n### Context\nSprint 1 shipped in v0.19.0 on 2026-04-21: built-in megaplan cloud subcommand (init/build/deploy/status/attach/logs/exec/resume/down/destroy) with a Railway provider, extracted from the ad-hoc setup at ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/. Spec schema lives in megaplan/cloud/spec.py, templates in megaplan/cloud/templates/, providers in megaplan/cloud/providers/.\n\nArchitectural principle established in sprint 1 and now codified: CORE megaplan owns capabilities, CLOUD subcommands are thin transport wrappers. Do not reinvent chain state parsing in cloud. Do not grow a parallel 'cloud chain *' surface. Core gets the command; cloud wraps it for remote execution.\n\n### Sprint 2 deliverables\n\nCore megaplan additions (must work locally without any cloud dependency):\n1. megaplan chain start --spec <path> \u2014 validate spec, resolve referenced idea files, kick auto-loop per milestone. Replaces the 'init + auto' pair for chain runs.\n2. megaplan chain status --spec <path> \u2014 read chain_state.json, pretty-print current_milestone, completed, remaining, per-milestone status. Unit tests against synthetic chain states.\n3. megaplan init --idea-file <path> with optional --auto-start flag \u2014 read idea from a file instead of the positional CLI arg.\n\nCloud additions (thin wrappers over the new core commands):\n4. megaplan cloud chain <spec.yaml> \u2014 upload spec, then cloud exec to call megaplan chain start remotely.\n5. megaplan cloud bootstrap <idea-file> \u2014 upload idea file, then cloud exec to call megaplan init --idea-file --auto-start remotely.\n6. megaplan cloud status --chain \u2014 fetch remote chain_state.json, invoke the core chain-status formatter on it. Do NOT reinvent the parser.\n\nNew providers:\n7. Local provider (docker compose) \u2014 fastest iteration target, no Railway/cloud dependency. Becomes the CI-friendly smoke-test target.\n8. SSH provider (plain docker-over-ssh) \u2014 'any host with docker + ssh access' story.\n\nToolchain extensibility:\n9. toolchains: block in cloud.yaml \u2014 declares one or more toolchains (rust, go, java, or custom with user-provided install snippet). Template renderer appends corresponding Dockerfile stages. Without this, the image is Python/Node only.\n\nHardening + retirement:\n10. Secret redaction in cloud logs output (match known secret name patterns, replace with ***REDACTED***).\n11. Clear error messages + documentation link when railway or docker CLI is missing at runtime.\n12. ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ migration \u2014 deploy cloud with a cloud.yaml matching reigh's current env, run a tiny plan to verify parity, then delete the folder and replace with a MIGRATED.md pointer.\n\n### Hard constraints\n- Core commands MUST work locally without any cloud code loaded.\n- Cloud wrappers MUST call out to core commands, not reimplement.\n- Fly provider is OPTIONAL (skip if time-pressured).\n- Preserve v0.19.0's public surface; this is additive.\n- No breaking cloud.yaml changes from v0.19.0 (add fields, don't rename).\n- Unit tests for every new core command; mocked-subprocess tests for every new provider; smoke test for local provider docker-compose lifecycle.\n\n### Explicit non-goals\n- No Kubernetes provider.\n- No chain-of-chains.\n- No cloud-specific chain status parser (the whole point of the core-first architecture).\n- No version bump in this plan \u2014 sprint 2 ships as v0.20.0 but the bump + CHANGELOG commit is a separate follow-up.\n\n### References\n- Sprint 1 landed in v0.19.0 (2026-04-21). Full CHANGELOG entry in CHANGELOG.md.\n- Reigh parity reference: ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ and megaplan/cloud/_reference/ (gitignored local copy of same).\n- Verified launcher: ./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan (system python is 3.8, fails on NotRequired).\n- Sprint 1 target retrospective: cloud subcommand CLI is already wired via megaplan/cloud/cli.py and dispatched from megaplan/cli.py.\n\nRobustness: standard \u2014 feature-rich with architecture decisions to enforce, multiple independent pieces worth independent critique, gate useful for scope discipline.",

Watch items to keep visible during execution:
- Validation Order step 7 has a known text-level mismatch (accepted tradeoff): plan writes `cloud bootstrap` + `cloud status --chain` via marker as a single sequence, but `cloud bootstrap` never writes a marker. At manual-E2E time, split into two disjoint sequences: (a) `cloud chain <spec>` → `cloud status --chain` via marker → `cloud destroy`, and (b) `cloud bootstrap <idea>` → `cloud status` (non-chain default) → `cloud destroy`.
- Marker location MUST be provider-independent: `~/.megaplan/cloud/markers/<sha256(abs_path_of_cloud.yaml)[:16]>/last_chain.json`. Railway uses TemporaryDirectory; writing the marker inside the deploy dir would silently evaporate. T7's `_marker_dir(cloud_yaml_path)` helper is the ONLY place this path is derived — both T15 and T16 must call it; don't open-code the path.
- argv normalization MUST be the first line of `main()` in `megaplan/cli.py`. `cli_entry()` calls `main(argv=None)`; without `if argv is None: argv = sys.argv[1:]` at entry, the lazy `argv[0] == 'cloud'` intercept never fires for shell invocations. `tests/test_cli_entry.py` regression-guards this — do not delete it.
- Core/cloud isolation is a grep-enforced invariant. No `megaplan.cloud.*` import may appear in any core module. No cloud module may reimplement chain-state parsing beyond calling `chain.load_chain_state` / `chain.load_spec` / `chain.format_chain_status`. T20's grep check enforces this.
- Public `cloud.yaml` surface from v0.19.0 must parse unchanged — every v0.19.0 spec loads with no change in parsed `CloudSpec` fields. All additions (local/ssh blocks, toolchains) are additive with defaults.
- With `toolchains:` OMITTED, the rendered Dockerfile must be byte-identical to the v0.19.0 baseline. This is a byte-diff test, not a semantic-equivalence test — trailing newlines, whitespace, and comment order all count.
- `cloud bootstrap --plan-name` is OPTIONAL. When omitted, the remote command must NOT include `--name` — delegate to core's slug-based default. When set, include `--name {shlex.quote(args.plan_name)}`.
- Every interpolated value in SSH provider argv and `ssh_exec` call sites must pass through `shlex.quote`. This is a shell-injection surface; tests should assert quoting with adversarial inputs containing spaces, quotes, and `$`.
- LocalProvider and SshProvider should each stay under ~200 LOC (soft budget). If you're trending longer, look for patterns to push into the base class rather than expanding the concrete provider.
- `--session` is Railway-only. T8's `Provider.supports_session: bool` class attribute gates it. Do NOT hardcode `provider.name == "railway"` checks elsewhere in the CLI.
- The attach handler has a documented redaction gap (interactive pty precludes line-buffered wrapping). T17 requires this gap be noted in the attach handler's docstring so maintainers don't assume parity with `logs -f`.
- Fly provider stays deferred. `provider: fly` must raise a distinct 'future provider' error (not the same error as an unknown provider). Test this in `tests/test_cloud_spec.py`.
- Reigh folder deletion is HUMAN-EXECUTED. T19 only drafts the runbook; do not auto-execute `rm -rf` against `~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/`. The safe ordering is: write `MIGRATED.md` FIRST, then `find -mindepth 1 ! -name MIGRATED.md -print0 | xargs -0 rm -rf` to preserve the pointer.

        Idea:
Sprint 2 of the megaplan cloud feature — extend core megaplan ergonomics, add local + ssh providers, ship toolchain extensibility in cloud.yaml, retire the old reigh-megaplan-dev folder.

### Context
Sprint 1 shipped in v0.19.0 on 2026-04-21: built-in megaplan cloud subcommand (init/build/deploy/status/attach/logs/exec/resume/down/destroy) with a Railway provider, extracted from the ad-hoc setup at ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/. Spec schema lives in megaplan/cloud/spec.py, templates in megaplan/cloud/templates/, providers in megaplan/cloud/providers/.

Architectural principle established in sprint 1 and now codified: CORE megaplan owns capabilities, CLOUD subcommands are thin transport wrappers. Do not reinvent chain state parsing in cloud. Do not grow a parallel 'cloud chain *' surface. Core gets the command; cloud wraps it for remote execution.

### Sprint 2 deliverables

Core megaplan additions (must work locally without any cloud dependency):
1. megaplan chain start --spec <path> — validate spec, resolve referenced idea files, kick auto-loop per milestone. Replaces the 'init + auto' pair for chain runs.
2. megaplan chain status --spec <path> — read chain_state.json, pretty-print current_milestone, completed, remaining, per-milestone status. Unit tests against synthetic chain states.
3. megaplan init --idea-file <path> with optional --auto-start flag — read idea from a file instead of the positional CLI arg.

Cloud additions (thin wrappers over the new core commands):
4. megaplan cloud chain <spec.yaml> — upload spec, then cloud exec to call megaplan chain start remotely.
5. megaplan cloud bootstrap <idea-file> — upload idea file, then cloud exec to call megaplan init --idea-file --auto-start remotely.
6. megaplan cloud status --chain — fetch remote chain_state.json, invoke the core chain-status formatter on it. Do NOT reinvent the parser.

New providers:
7. Local provider (docker compose) — fastest iteration target, no Railway/cloud dependency. Becomes the CI-friendly smoke-test target.
8. SSH provider (plain docker-over-ssh) — 'any host with docker + ssh access' story.

Toolchain extensibility:
9. toolchains: block in cloud.yaml — declares one or more toolchains (rust, go, java, or custom with user-provided install snippet). Template renderer appends corresponding Dockerfile stages. Without this, the image is Python/Node only.

Hardening + retirement:
10. Secret redaction in cloud logs output (match known secret name patterns, replace with ***REDACTED***).
11. Clear error messages + documentation link when railway or docker CLI is missing at runtime.
12. ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ migration — deploy cloud with a cloud.yaml matching reigh's current env, run a tiny plan to verify parity, then delete the folder and replace with a MIGRATED.md pointer.

### Hard constraints
- Core commands MUST work locally without any cloud code loaded.
- Cloud wrappers MUST call out to core commands, not reimplement.
- Fly provider is OPTIONAL (skip if time-pressured).
- Preserve v0.19.0's public surface; this is additive.
- No breaking cloud.yaml changes from v0.19.0 (add fields, don't rename).
- Unit tests for every new core command; mocked-subprocess tests for every new provider; smoke test for local provider docker-compose lifecycle.

### Explicit non-goals
- No Kubernetes provider.
- No chain-of-chains.
- No cloud-specific chain status parser (the whole point of the core-first architecture).
- No version bump in this plan — sprint 2 ships as v0.20.0 but the bump + CHANGELOG commit is a separate follow-up.

### References
- Sprint 1 landed in v0.19.0 (2026-04-21). Full CHANGELOG entry in CHANGELOG.md.
- Reigh parity reference: ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ and megaplan/cloud/_reference/ (gitignored local copy of same).
- Verified launcher: ./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan (system python is 3.8, fails on NotRequired).
- Sprint 1 target retrospective: cloud subcommand CLI is already wired via megaplan/cloud/cli.py and dispatched from megaplan/cli.py.

Robustness: standard — feature-rich with architecture decisions to enforce, multiple independent pieces worth independent critique, gate useful for scope discipline.

(1) **Step 4 argv normalization (FLAG-008, correctness)**: add `if argv is None: argv = sys.argv[1:]` as the first line of `main()` so the lazy `argv[0] == \"cloud\"` intercept fires on normal shell invocations via `cli_entry()`. Added `tests/test_cli_entry.py` to regression-guard the entrypoint path. (2) **Steps 7 + 15 + 16 marker location (FLAG-006, callers, issue_hints, issue_hints-1)**: introduced `_marker_dir(cloud_yaml_path)` \u2192 `~/.megaplan/cloud/markers/<sha256-of-abs-path>[:16]/` as a provider-independent location for `last_chain.json`. This decouples the marker from the deploy dir, so Railway's `TemporaryDirectory` flow no longer loses the ad-hoc chain reference between `cloud chain` and `cloud status --chain`. Step 16's precedence now reads from `_marker_dir(...)`, not the deploy dir. Gate's recommended key derivation (SHA of `cloud.yaml` absolute path) adopted verbatim to match the \"one deploy dir per cloud.yaml\" mental model. Everything else from Rev 3 is verbatim. No scope creep \u2014 both changes map directly to the gate's stated two one-liners.",
  "flags_addressed": [
    "FLAG-006",
    "FLAG-008",
    "callers",
    "correctness",
    "issue_hints",
    "issue_hints-1"
  ],
  "questions": [
    "Marker key derivation \u2014 using `sha256(str(Path(cloud.yaml).resolve()))[:16]` matches gate's 'one marker per cloud.yaml deployment' suggestion. Should we add a `cloud init --force` side-effect that also clears the marker dir for the derived SHA, or leave that as a manual `rm` step? I've assumed manual cleanup; markers are durable by design so users can inspect them after `destroy`.",
    "argv normalization \u2014 the fix to `main(argv=None)` is at the function entry, before the lazy cloud intercept. Should we also add defensive handling for the case where a test passes `argv=[]` explicitly (currently fine: the `if argv and argv[0] == 'cloud'` guard is falsy for empty lists, so argparse handles it normally)? I've assumed the current guard is sufficient.",
    "Marker file path in docs/cloud.md \u2014 document the full `~/.megaplan/cloud/markers/<sha>/last_chain.json` path so users can inspect/debug, or mention only the logical location and hide the SHA derivation? I've assumed full disclosure since it helps with debugging; users aren't expected to write the path by hand."
  ],
